A successful kitchen remodel starts long before the first cabinet is removed. Careful planning can help you create a kitchen that looks great, functions efficiently, and fits the way you use your home. Before starting your kitchen renovation, consider: • Your layout: Think about how you move between cooking, cleaning, dining, and storage areas. • Storage needs: Plan cabinets, drawers, pantry space, and organization around your everyday needs. • Materials: Choose countertops, flooring, cabinets, and fixtures based on both appearance and durability. • Lighting: Combine task, ambient, and accent lighting to make the kitchen more comfortable and functional. • Appliances: Consider appliance placement and how new equipment will work with your overall layout. • Budget and timeline: Establish realistic expectations before construction begins. At 4 Edges Construction, we provide kitchen remodeling services throughout Vacaville, Fairfield, Napa, Davis, Dixon, and Sacramento. Our team works with homeowners to plan and build kitchens that combine functionality, craftsmanship, and a design that fits their needs. Thinking about remodeling your kitchen? Start with a plan that works for your home and your lifestyle.

From the owner
Restore Your Cabinets in Walnut Creek Many Walnut Creek homes were built with genuinely good cabinetry. Before you spend on replacement, let us show you exactly what professional refinishing can do for what you already own. Adval Construction Inc removes and labels every door and drawer front, strips or sands the existing finish, repairs chips, dents and water marks, re glues loose joints, tightens or replaces hinges and rebuilds whatever needs rebuilding. Then we spray professional primers and finish coats for a smooth, even, factory quality surface with no brush strokes and no roller texture anywhere. You can return to a richer version of the original wood tone, or move to a fully modern painted finish. Either way you keep solid construction that is often better than what is sold in stores today, and you avoid the cost, the waste and the long timeline of a full replacement. We contain dust, ventilate properly and keep the project organized so your home stays livable from start to finish, with your kitchen usable through most of the schedule. Licensed contractor CSLB 1059130, fully insured, available 24/7. Book your free Walnut Creek cabinet assessment today and get an honest recommendation on whether to refinish, reface or replace.

From the owner
Not every renovation we do has a homeowner on the other end. Last year BGW Construction partnered with Kingsway Christian Church in Avon, Indiana to build a safe space for the Department of Child Services. When DCS removes a child from a home, that child needs somewhere safe to go. We converted 2,000 square feet inside the church into a space that looks and feels like a home. Full kitchen remodel. Full bathroom. Half bath refresh. Laundry hookup. And custom built-in bunk beds for the kids to sleep in. The scope was significant. We located the subsurface main sewer line four feet deep below the slab and handled extensive rough plumbing throughout. A comparable renovation with this kind of scope, including a full kitchen, bathroom, plumbing, and a custom built-in system, would typically run $120,000 to $150,000. We completed it for $80,000. That included the furniture. Lowe's in Avon provided much of the material at cost. Plainfield Christian Church made a generous donation. And skilled craftsmen and women donated their labor because they fell in love with what this project was for. That's what community renovation looks like when the project matters more than the margin. #BGWConstruction #AvonIndiana #designbuild #communityproject #dreambuilding

From the owner
Adding square footage to a home sounds straightforward until a contractor pulls back the curtain. Most homeowners walk into the first conversation carrying assumptions that are either outdated, borrowed from a neighbor's project, or simply wrong. Those assumptions cost money and time. The myths below are the ones Brother & Brother Builders hears most often from San Jose, CA homeowners before work begins, and clearing them up early makes the entire process go smoother for everyone. Myth: A Simple Addition Does Not Require a Permit This one causes real damage. Some homeowners believe that adding a bedroom over a garage or bumping out a family room a few feet is too minor to trigger permit requirements. It is not. In San Jose, CA, any structural addition to a home requires a building permit, a site plan review, and inspections at multiple stages. Skipping that process does not just risk a fine. It can void homeowner's insurance coverage, create title problems when the property sells, and force a demolition order if the work does not meet code. The permit timeline is often the biggest shock. Depending on the scope, permit approval in the South Bay can take six to fourteen weeks before a shovel touches the ground. From the owner
Wondering what your kitchen remodel will actually cost? The answer starts with square footage. A 10x10 kitchen (100 sq ft) typically runs $15,300 to $16,050 for budget updates, $25,500 to $32,100 for mid-range work, and $55,000 or more for high-end finishes. Move up to a 12x20 kitchen (240 sq ft) and budget tiers rise to $25,000-$30,000, mid-range to $50,000-$75,000, and high-end projects to $100,000-$140,000. Interestingly, cost per square foot actually drops as kitchens get bigger. That's because fixed costs like permits, plumbing rough-in, and labor mobilization stay roughly the same no matter the size, so they make up a smaller share of the total in larger kitchens. Appliances behave the same way, costing about the same whether your kitchen is 100 or 300 square feet. What does scale directly with size is flooring, cabinetry, and countertops, priced by square footage or linear wall footage. Layout shape matters too. A galley kitchen keeps cabinet runs minimal, while U-shaped kitchens and open-concept conversions push costs higher due to added cabinetry, structural work, or wall removal. In Dallas, remodels commonly run above $200 per square foot once labor and finishes are factored in. Whether you're planning a cosmetic refresh or a full layout change, knowing your kitchen's square footage is the fastest way to build a realistic starting budget before reaching out to a contractor. Contact us for a personalized estimate tailored to your kitchen's size and layout.

How long does it take to build a room addition? A room addition often takes several months from design to finish, with many projects falling near four to twelve months depending on size, permits, and site needs. Early work includes a floor plan, budget goals, and a check of how the new space joins the home. Plans often need review for permits. Next, crews may handle footings, framing, roofing, and weather protection. Wiring, heating, plumbing, and insulation follow as the design calls for them. Drywall, trim, flooring, and painting come later in the process. Delays can come from design changes, material lead times, weather, or hidden issues once work starts. A small room differs from a two-story build. Ask for a phase-by-phase schedule with key choices marked in advance. To help with planning, decide which features are must-haves before plans are sent for review. That can help limit late changes. Call to review your room addition plans and timeline.

From the owner
Drywall Finish Levels: What Each One Actually Means Not all drywall is finished the same way. The level of finish determines how smooth your walls read, how light travels across them, and which paints and textures will work. Here's the progression: LEVEL 1 - TAPE & BED. Joints are taped and bedded in compound, with the excess left in place. The fastest, most basic stage, and the right call only for walls nobody will ever see. LEVEL 2 - TAPE & FLOAT. Joints are smoothed and every screw and nail spot is covered. A sound, serviceable base when texture or a heavy paint will carry the final look. LEVEL 3 - TAPE, FLOAT & SKIM COAT. A skim coat goes across the surface to even out imperfections. The starting point for a truly smooth wall, and well suited to flat and eggshell paints. LEVEL 4 - TAPE, FLOAT, SKIM & SAND. That skim coat is sanded out to a tighter, more uniform plane. Worth the extra step when low-sheen paint will pick up any waviness in the wall. LEVEL 5 - FULLY FINISHED. Refined to a mirror-smooth surface with no visible seams anywhere. This is what high-gloss paint, dramatic lighting and premium interiors demand. Which level is right for your home comes down to lighting, paint sheen, budget, and the level your plans specify. We'll walk you through it before a single sheet goes up. Open-Concept Kitchen, Dining & Living Room Transformation This home had beautiful potential, but a closed-off layout held it back. The kitchen, dining room, and living room were divided by walls, leaving the space feeling cramped, with too little storage to keep up with everyday life. Our goal was simple: open it up and make every square foot work harder. We removed the dividing walls to create a bright, seamless open-concept space where cooking, dining, and relaxing all flow together. Behind the scenes, we completely redesigned the electrical system throughout the area and relocated the plumbing to fit the new layout, giving the refrigerator, sink, and a brand-new coffee bar exactly where they make the most sense. The heart of the new space is a set of custom cabinets designed around how this family actually lives, including a dedicated coffee bar and smart storage solutions that finally give everything a place. The cabinetry is topped with Calacatta Zurich quartz countertops, with a matching full-height backsplash cut from the same stone for a clean, continuous, high-end look. To tie it all together, we installed new flooring across the entire 1,600 sq ft first floor and finished the walls with fresh drywall and paint, so the whole level feels like one cohesive, modern home. The result: a spacious, light-filled layout with abundant storage, a kitchen built for both daily routines and entertaining, and a first floor that feels completely new.

From the owner
The left photo is the part that decides the right one. Those openings were framed into the wall while it was open, blocked on every side, and closed in before any tile went near them. A niche cannot be added later. It is a hole through a wall, so it has to miss the studs, the plumbing and anything else running in the bay behind. That is why we ask early where you want it and how big, and why the answer is often not where you first pointed. Height is worth thinking about too. A niche set at eye level is convenient and it is also the first thing anyone sees walking into the room, so it usually wants to line up with a grout joint in the field rather than float wherever it landed. Here the openings became four small boxes instead of one long shelf, each lined with a mosaic that would have been too busy across a whole wall and reads as a deliberate accent in a small space. The other thing that photo shows is the pan, floated and sloped before anything decorative happened. Order matters in a shower. Structure, then slope, then waterproofing, then tile. Tap Learn more and we will mark the niches on your wall before we frame. https://realdealbuildersinc.com/locations/valencia/tile-work/

Great Italian design has never stopped at the kitchen door. In Italy, the kitchen, the living room, the bathroom and the bedroom have always been conceived as chapters of the same story. Today that story has a new, powerful chapter: Arrital, the kitchen brand at the heart of our collection, and Busnelli, one of Italy's most celebrated names in sofas and upholstered seating, now belong to the same family — the WeDo Home division of the Italian group WeDo Holding. For our clients in Palm Springs and Silicon Valley, this is far more than industry news. It is the confirmation of a direction Tredi Interiors has been following for years: to work not as a cabinet dealer, but as a true Italian design studio for the entire house — from the first sketch of the kitchen island to the last cushion on the sofa. In this article, we explain who WeDo Home is, why the pairing of Arrital and Busnelli is so meaningful, and how it allows us to continue and improve our vision of complete, coherent modern interior design. Arrital AK_Project — the kitchen as the architectural centre of an open-plan home. One Group, One Vision: Who Is WeDo Home?
